message.content:
**Proteins commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Function | Representative Examples | |----------|-----------|------------------------| | **Integral (Trans‑membrane)** | Span the bilayer; form pores/transport pathways | • Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase
• Glucose transporter GLUT1 / GLUT4
• Aquaporin‑1
• Voltage‑gated K⁺ channel Kv11.1
• Connexin43 (gap junctions)
• Caveolin‑1 (caveolae) | | **Peripheral (Surface‑associated)** | Attach to inner leaflet or other membrane components; often signal transduction | • G‑protein–coupled receptors (β₂‑adrenergic, rhodopsin)
• Receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR, HER2)
• Integrins (α5β1, αvβ3)
• Cadherins (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• CD45 phosphatase (T‑cell surface marker) | | **Lipid‑anchored** | Covalently attached to lipids rather than spanning the bilayer | • Squalene synthase (prenylation site)
• Hedgehog signaling ligand (cholesterol‑modified)
• Ras family small GTPases (farnesylated) | | **Extracellular matrix connectors** | Link cells to ECM via proteoglycan interactions | • Fibronectin receptor (integrin β1)
• Collagen-binding discoidin domain receptors (DDR1/DDR2) | ### Quick Takeaways * **Ion channels & pumps** keep ions moving across the membrane. * **Transporters** shuttle nutrients/metabolites (e.g., glucose). * **Receptors** sense hormones, neurotransmitters, growth factors. * **Adhesion molecules** mediate cell–cell and cell–matrix contacts. * **Gap junction proteins** allow direct intercellular communication. These proteins together give the plasma membrane its dynamic roles—selective permeability, signal reception/transmission, structural integrity, and interaction with the extracellular environment.
